title: SART: Sign-Absolute Reformulation Theory for Binary Variable Reduction in Neural Network Verification
abstract: arXiv:2611.18657v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Complete formal verification of neural networks is crucial for their deployment in safety-critical domains. A key bottleneck stems from encoding complexity: traditional methods assign one binary variable per unstable ReLU neuron. We propose the Sign-Absolute Reformulation Theory (SART), which fundamentally breaks the conventional one-to-one mapping between unstable neurons and binary variables by establishing formal reducibility criteria. This allows for finer-grained modeling, where each unstable neuron corresponds on average to fewer than one binary variable, thereby reducing verification complexity at its source. Based on SART, we derive a theoretical lower bound on the number of binary variables required for complete verification and, under the assumption that $P \neq NP$, prove that variables in the final layer can be compressed by 50\%, while the number of variables in intermediate layers cannot be further reduced. translated_title: SART：用于神经网络验证中二元变量缩减的符号-绝对值重构理论
translated_abstract: 神经网络的完全形式化验证对于其在安全关键领域的部署至关重要。一个关键瓶颈源于编码复杂度：传统方法为每个不稳定的ReLU神经元分配一个二元变量。我们提出了符号-绝对值重构理论（SART），通过建立形式化的可约减性判据，从根本上打破了不稳定神经元与二元变量之间传统的一对一映射关系。这使得更细粒度的建模成为可能，每个不稳定神经元平均对应少于一个二元变量，从而从源头上降低了验证复杂度。基于SART，我们推导出了完全验证所需二元变量数量的理论下界，并在P≠NP的假设下，证明最后一层的变量可以压缩50%，而中间层的变量数量无法进一步约减。
tldr: 提出符号-绝对值重构理论（SART），打破了不稳定ReLU神经元与二元变量之间的一对一映射关系，从源头上降低神经网络完全验证的编码复杂度，并推导出变量数量的理论下界，证明最后一层变量可压缩50%。
en_tdlr: Proposes the Sign-Absolute Reformulation Theory (SART), which breaks the one-to-one mapping between unstable ReLU neurons and binary variables, fundamentally reducing encoding complexity in complete neural network verification and deriving a theoretical lower bound proving 50% variable compression in the final layer.
